scope: Resolve the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass's deferred follow-up: find the consumer-side of the battle-effect queue (queued by FUN_005901D0 BCS-Y-0412 BattleResultQueuePush at producer end). That analysis partially answered the CharaActionController.enqueue chain question - finding a queue/poll boundary rather than direct call. This completes the picture by finding the polling consumer.

method.step1: Re-check existing catalog for FUN_0058A090 (CharaActionStateTickProcessor BCS-Y-1000). Notes mention 2 callers: FUN_0058B2A0 (case 0xCE handler) + FUN_0058DF90 (TBD - 'likely the actor tick loop entry'). FUN_0058DF90 was uncataloged - decomp candidate.
method.step2: Decomp FUN_0058DF90 (299B): 20-callee chain. Calls in order: FUN_00586150 (conditional, +0x26d bit clear), FUN_00585D70, FUN_0058A090 (action-state tick), FUN_005861B0 (status-effect tick), FUN_0058DA10 (battle-effect queue drain - THE CONSUMER), FUN_0058B1B0, FUN_0058AEF0, FUN_005893F0, build local 0x10-byte record + broadcast subtype 0x1E via FUN_004D7980, FUN_0058A8E0, FUN_00588ED0, FUN_00588F60, +0x264 state read, FUN_004D86B0 self-check, broadcast subtype 0x1E, vtable[19]+vtable[13] dispatch on actor+0xBA0. CONFIRMED: this IS the per-actor frame tick. 0 instruction-level callers (called via vtable from frame loop).
method.step3: Decomp FUN_0058DA10 (412B): the BATTLE-EFFECT QUEUE DRAIN. Body: if (actor+0xa90 == 0) return (empty queue check); read head cursor from actor+0xa8c, modulo against capacity at +0xa88; fetch entry pointer from queue array at actor+0xa84+head*4; switch on entry+4 (entry type 0..0x19) with 3 post-processing buckets: (a) cases 0-2: FUN_005901D0(entry) + broadcast subtype 3 or 4 via FUN_004D7980, (b) cases 3-0xb: FUN_005901D0 + broadcast subtype 4 + FUN_007C5600/FUN_0058CA80/FUN_0058A010 animation-trigger chain, (c) cases 0xc-0x19: FUN_005901D0 + broadcast variants. Advance head, decrement count, return.
method.step4: Decomp adjacent tick sub-helpers from FUN_0058DF90: FUN_00585D70 (173B - combat-status snapshot copy at actor+0xb24 + status broadcast subtype 8), FUN_00586150 (38B - combat-status flag clear loop, 6 fields at +0x290/0x2c0/0x2f0), FUN_005861B0 (733B - status-effect timer-decrement tick with 6 timer slots, per-slot broadcast subtypes a/b/c/d/e). FUN_005861B0 is the per-frame status-effect tick (sibling of action-state and battle-effect ticks).
method.step5: Architectural synthesis: the per-frame actor tick (FUN_0058DF90) is a TRIPLE-TICK function running three independent ticks on each Chara actor per frame: (1) combat-status snapshot tick (FUN_00585D70), (2) action-state machine tick (FUN_0058A090 BCS-Y-1000), (3) status-effect timer tick (FUN_005861B0), (4) BATTLE-EFFECT QUEUE DRAIN (FUN_0058DA10). The queue drain is the missing consumer that the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass hypothesized. The 0x00DA pipeline now completes: wire arrival -> FUN_005901D0 producer push to queue -> next frame: FUN_0058DA10 drain pops entry -> per-type handler calls FUN_005901D0 AGAIN (re-process or detail-apply) -> animation chain FUN_007C5600/FUN_0058CA80/FUN_0058A010 for entries in type-range 3-0xb.

key_findings: FUN_0058DA10 is the BATTLE-EFFECT QUEUE CONSUMER - the missing-link consumer that the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass hypothesized as a 'queue/poll boundary'. Per-frame called from FUN_0058DF90 actor tick. Drains one entry per call from circular buffer at actor+0xa84..+0xa90 (4-field queue layout). Closes the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass's open question on the CharaActionController.enqueue chain.

FUN_0058DF90 is the per-actor frame TICK ENTRY. 299-byte triple-tick function calling 4 distinct per-frame ticks: combat-status snapshot (FUN_00585D70), action-state machine (FUN_0058A090 BCS-Y-1000), status-effect timer (FUN_005861B0), battle-effect queue drain (FUN_0058DA10). Single tick orchestrator for Chara actor per-frame state evolution. 0 instruction-level callers - called via vtable from the engine frame loop.

Battle-effect queue layout (clarified): actor+0xa84 = array base (pointer), +0xa88 = capacity, +0xa8c = head cursor (wraps at capacity), +0xa90 = current count. Per-entry slot is 4 bytes (entry pointer) - actual entry contents are heap-allocated 0x1A0-byte records per BCS-S-0031. Drain pops one entry per frame (not all queued entries).

Entry-type dispatch in FUN_0058DA10: switch on entry+4 byte covers 26 types (0..0x19) routed to 3 post-process buckets. Bucket 0-2 (3 types): simple broadcast (subtype 3 or 4). Bucket 3-0xb (9 types): animation-trigger path with FUN_007C5600/FUN_0058CA80/FUN_0058A010 chain - likely the actual CharaActionController.enqueue equivalent. Bucket 0xc-0x19 (14 types): variant broadcasts. The animation trigger is type-gated.

FUN_005901D0 has DUAL role: producer (named BattleResultQueuePush per BCS-Y-0412) and consumer entry-processor (called per-entry in FUN_0058DA10 drain). The 'push' attribution describes the s2c reception path; the per-entry call in the drain is the apply/process side. The unmapped-payload-decoding pass's naming is misleading - the function is more accurately 'BattleEffectEntryProcess' with both push and per-frame-apply call sites. Naming cleanup candidate.

Status-effect tick (FUN_005861B0, 733B) is a SEPARATE subsystem from battle effects. Walks 6 timer slots at actor+0x290..+0x2c0..+0x2f0, decrements timers, broadcasts state changes per timer per subtype (a/b/c/d/e). Independent of the battle-effect queue. Was historically conflated with battle-effect logic.

Combat-status snapshot (FUN_00585D70, 173B) reads from actor+0xb24 region into local 0x74-byte snapshot, copies to actor+0xaac, sets dirty +0xb20, broadcasts subtype 8. Targets the SAME 28-slot dword table at actor+0xaac that the 0x00D6-state-flag-pipeline pass's cases 0xD6/0xD7 wrote to - the snapshot consumer + the wire-receive path BOTH update the same table on Chara actors.

Closes the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass's deferred follow-up: the s2c-to-animation chain for 0x00DA is now end-to-end attributable. Wire arrival -> FUN_0058CCA0 case 0xDA -> FUN_0058CAD0 -> FUN_0058C690 -> BattleResultEffectVisualClassSelector (the unmapped-payload-decoding pass) -> LogEntryBuilder (BCS-Y-1009) -> LogEntryDispatcher / BattleResultQueuePush (BCS-Y-0412) PRODUCER -> queue at actor+0xa84 -> [next frame] -> FUN_0058DF90 actor tick -> FUN_0058DA10 drain pops entry -> per-type animation chain via FUN_007C5600/FUN_0058CA80/FUN_0058A010.

Calls 4 independent ticks in sequence: (1) combat-status snapshot [[CharaElement_CombatStatusSnapshot_FUN_00585D70]], (2) action-state machine tick [[CharaActionStateTickProcessor_FUN_0058A090]] (BCS-Y-1000), (3) status-effect timer tick [[CharaElement_StatusEffectTimerTick_FUN_005861B0]], (4) battle-effect queue drain [[CharaElement_BattleEffectQueueDrain_FUN_0058DA10]]. Also broadcasts subtype 0x1E via FUN_004D7980, sets +0x264 stamp, calls vtable[19]+vtable[13] on actor+0xBA0 (Lua object). 0 instruction-level callers - reached via vtable dispatch from engine frame loop. Resolves the chara-action-state-pipeline pass's TBD on FUN_0058A090's second caller. This architectural finding.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaElement_BattleEffectQueueDrain_FUN_0058DA10
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 412-byte battle-effect QUEUE CONSUMER. Per-frame called from [[CharaElement_PerActorFrameTick_FUN_0058DF90]]. Drains one entry per call from circular buffer at actor+0xa84 (array base) +0xa88 (capacity) +0xa8c (head cursor) +0xa90 (count). Returns early if queue empty. Switches on entry+4 byte (entry type 0..0x19): cases 0-2 simple broadcast (subtype 3/4); cases 3-0xb ANIMATION TRIGGER PATH via FUN_007C5600 + FUN_0058CA80 + FUN_0058A010 (this is the consumer side of CharaActionController.enqueue per the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass); cases 0xc-0x19 variant broadcasts. All cases call FUN_005901D0 (BCS-Y-0412 per-entry apply, dual-role with the producer path). Resolves the 0x00DA-pipeline-synthesis pass's deferred consumer-side question.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaElement_CombatStatusSnapshot_FUN_00585D70
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 173-byte combat-status snapshot copier in the per-actor frame tick chain. If actor+0xb24 != 0 (pending snapshot pointer), reads via FUN_0055D2B0 into local 0x74-byte stack snapshot, copies 0x1D dwords to actor+0xaac (the SAME 28-slot dword table written by the 0x00D6-state-flag-pipeline pass's cases 0xD6/0xD7), sets dirty +0xb20=1, clears +0xb24. If dirty bit set: broadcasts subtype 8 via FUN_004D7980 + FUN_00585930 + sets +0x26d bit 6. Combat-status broadcast variant. Sole caller [[CharaElement_PerActorFrameTick_FUN_0058DF90]].

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaElement_StatusEffectTimerTick_FUN_005861B0
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 733-byte status-effect TIMER TICK. Walks 6 status-effect timer slots at actor+0x290..+0x2c0..+0x2f0 (3 rows of 2 slots, 0x48 byte stride). Per-slot: tracks max remaining timer across 3 sub-timers per slot; decrements active timer by per-tick rate at slot+1; on changes, builds a per-slot state record sized 4/0xc/0x28/0x14/0x10 by switch on slot bits 1-3 (type discriminator) and broadcasts via FUN_004D7980 with subtype 10..0xe (one per slot variant). Sole caller [[CharaElement_PerActorFrameTick_FUN_0058DF90]]. Separate subsystem from battle-effect queue (FUN_0058DA10) - status effects are timer-based, not event-queue-based.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaElement_CombatStatusClearLoop_FUN_00586150
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: 38-byte combat-status bit-0 clear loop. Walks 6 status fields at actor+(0x2a8/0x2c0/0x2d8) (2 iterations of 3 stride-0x48 entries each), clears bit 0 of each (the bit 0 = 'active' flag). Called from [[CharaElement_PerActorFrameTick_FUN_0058DF90]] only when (+0x26d & 0x40) AND (+0x26d & 4) - a specific dual-condition gate. Also called from FUN_005877E0 (other context). Likely a 'reset all status flags' helper for a specific state transition.
